papers.title: mapfx.norm: a method for removing unwanted variation from massively parallel cytometry data.
papers.abstract: Massively parallel cytometry (MPC) experiments allow cost-effective quantification of >200 surface proteins at single-cell resolution. The Infinity Flow protocol was developed to measure highly informative protein 'Backbone' markers on all cells in wells distributed across plates, along with well-specific exploratory protein 'Infinity' markers. Backbone markers are then used to impute the Infinity markers using machine learning methods. This protocol offers unprecedented opportunities for more comprehensive classification of cell types. However, the protocol can be improved, particularly in re
papers.summary: The paper introduces mapfx.norm, a normalization method designed to remove unwanted technical variation from massively parallel cytometry data, specifically for the Infinity Flow protocol that measures over 200 surface proteins at single-cell resolution. By correcting batch effects and other artifacts, the method improves the accuracy of imputing exploratory 'Infinity' markers from backbone markers using machine learning, enabling more reliable cell-type classification.

papers.title: Biophysically grounded deep learning improves protein-protein ΔΔG prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in protein-protein binding free energy (ΔΔG) remains limited by small, redundant datasets and train-test homology leakage. We show that commonly used SKEMPI2 splits inflate model performance, with every tested AI predictor declining under a stringent split that controls homology at the level of individual chains (60% sequence identity). We introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that integrates five residue-level biophysical descriptors into pretrained protein representations through cross-embedding attention. Under leakage-controlled evaluation,
papers.summary: The authors show that standard SKEMPI2 train-test splits leak homology and inflate the apparent accuracy of AI models for predicting mutation-induced changes in protein-protein binding affinity (ΔΔG). They introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that injects five residue-level biophysical descriptors into pretrained protein representations via cross-embedding attention, and demonstrate improved performance under a stringent homology-controlled split (60% sequence identity at the chain level).

papers.title: Protein sequence domain annotation using a language model.
papers.abstract: Protein domain annotation underlies large-scale functional inference and is commonly performed by scanning sequences against libraries of profile hidden Markov models (profile HMMs). We describe PSALM, a protein domain annotation method that combines (i) a pretrained protein language model (ESM-2) with (ii) a per-residue domain-state classifier and (iii) a structured probabilistic decoder that produces a single, non-overlapping set of domain calls with explicit boundaries and scores. On a benchmark of 76.9M protein sequences with 107M annotated domains, PSALM attains a domain-detection sensiti
papers.summary: PSALM is a new protein domain annotation method that combines a pretrained protein language model (ESM-2) with a per-residue domain-state classifier and a structured probabilistic decoder to produce non-overlapping domain calls with explicit boundaries and scores. Benchmarked on 76.9M sequences with 107M annotated domains, it improves domain-detection sensitivity over profile-HMM scanning. This offers a language-model-based alternative to the standard HMMER-style annotation pipeline.

papers.title: CoEVFold suite: User friendly pipelines to visually represent protein coevolution.
papers.abstract: Multiple sequence alignment (MSA) data underlies current principles in protein folding and protein-protein interaction prediction, from which deep-learning models trained on protein sequence and structure datasets can predict protein structure. However, what is missing are user-friendly tools that enable researchers to identify and visualise coevolution, the principal signal that these MSAs encode. Here we present tools to identify and visualize coevolution, through a pipeline (CoEVFold) that uses basic direct coupling algorithms derived from GREMLIN and an input alignment of sequences from MM
papers.summary: The authors present CoEVFold, a user-friendly software suite that identifies and visualizes coevolutionary signals from multiple sequence alignments of proteins. It implements direct coupling analysis algorithms derived from GREMLIN, making it easier for researchers to inspect the coevolutionary signal that underlies protein structure and interaction prediction. The suite is aimed at lowering the barrier to entry for visualizing coevolution without requiring deep computational expertise.

papers.title: Chemical profiling, bioactivity, and machine learning-supported target analysis of Euphorbia macroclada extracts from aerial parts and roots.
papers.abstract: Euphorbia macroclada is used in Anatolian folk medicine, but its chemistry and bioactivity have not been compared across plant parts and extraction solvents. We extracted aerial parts and roots with ethyl acetate, acetone, 70% aqueous acetone and water. The extracts were then profiled by LC-MS/MS and tested in antioxidant and enzyme inhibition assays. UHPLC-ESI-Orbitrap-MS/MS analysis showed 101 compounds, mainly flavonoids, hydrolysable tannins, coumarins, and phenolic acid derivatives. The aqueous acetone extracts had the highest phenolic content (up to 86.94 mg GAE per g, roots) and the str
papers.summary: This study profiled extracts from the aerial parts and roots of Euphorbia macroclada using LC-MS/MS, identifying 101 compounds (mainly flavonoids, tannins, coumarins, and phenolic acids) and comparing antioxidant and enzyme inhibition activities across solvents. Aqueous acetone extracts showed the highest phenolic content, and machine learning was used to support target analysis. The work provides a comparative chemical and bioactivity map of this folk-medicinal plant.

papers.title: Association of Estimated Insulin Sensitivity With Cardiovascular Disease in Individuals Without Diabetes: Use of Traditional and Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: The predictive role of the Estimated Insulin Sensitivity (e-IS) index, serving as a surrogate marker for insulin resistance, in cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mechanisms remains underexplored in nondiabetic populations. We aimed to evaluate the association of e-IS with CVD incidence and its predictive utility for CVD risk.
papers.summary: This study examines whether an estimated insulin sensitivity (e-IS) index, a surrogate marker for insulin resistance, predicts incident cardiovascular disease in people without diabetes. It compares traditional statistical models with machine learning approaches to assess the index's predictive utility for CVD risk.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Aided Design of Peptides with Custom Secondary Structure Motifs and Reduced Amino Acid Alphabets.
papers.abstract: Proteins are highly diverse functional polymers where the specific sequence of amino acids, selected from a standard genetically encoded alphabet of 20 (C20), determines the structure and ultimately the function of the resulting folded protein. This standard alphabet has been identified to be nonrandomly distributed in physicochemical properties crucial to both structure formation and function, often referred to as coverage theory. While machine learning models have drastically improved protein structure prediction, success of protein design models lags structure prediction, particularly for c
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: This paper presents an AI-aided method for designing peptides that fold into specific secondary structure motifs while using reduced amino acid alphabets (fewer than the standard 20 amino acids). The approach leverages machine learning to generate custom peptide sequences, showing that functional structural motifs can be encoded with simplified chemical repertoires. This has implications for synthetic biology and peptide engineering where reduced alphabets may simplify design and synthesis.

papers.title: Natural Language Processing Supported by Annotation Process Artifacts to Detect Risky Alcohol Use in Electronic Health Records: Algorithm Development and Validation Study.
papers.abstract: High-risk alcohol use and alcohol use disorder (AUD) are significant contributors to surgical risk and complications yet remain underidentified in surgical populations. While electronic health records (EHRs) contain relevant information about patients' alcohol use in clinical notes, manual chart review is time-intensive and impractical at scale. Natural language processing (NLP) offers a path to automated identification, but alcohol-related risk classes are highly imbalanced in clinical populations, making multiclass classification particularly challenging.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates an NLP algorithm that leverages annotation process artifacts to detect risky alcohol use in electronic health records, addressing the challenge of highly imbalanced multiclass classification in surgical populations. The approach aims to automate identification of high-risk alcohol use and AUD from clinical notes, which are currently underidentified despite their relevance to surgical risk.

papers.title: RNAcomp2D: a web tool to execute multiple methods and visually compare predictions of RNA secondary structure.
papers.abstract: Ribonucleic acids (RNAs) are involved in many important biological processes. In particular, non-coding RNAs are crucial regulators of cellular processes, playing a significant role in gene expression. RNA secondary structure is key to infer their specific function and for understanding how they interact with other molecules. Many computational models have been developed in the last decade to predict the secondary structure, achieving increasingly higher success rates. However, each new method has its own input-output interface, programming language, computational requirements and, sometimes,
papers.summary: RNAcomp2D is a web tool that lets users run multiple RNA secondary structure prediction methods through a single interface and visually compare their outputs side by side. It addresses the fragmentation of the field, where each prediction method has its own input/output format, language, and computational requirements, making benchmarking and method selection difficult for non-specialists.

papers.title: Phenotypic expansion of TUBGCP6 primary microcephaly: severe cortical malformations without chorioretinopathy and insights into variant interpretation.
papers.abstract: Biallelic variants of TUBGCP6 are associated with primary microcephaly, chorioretinopathy, short stature, and intellectual disability (ID). Most reported cases had at least one loss-of-function variant.
papers.summary: This paper expands the known clinical spectrum of TUBGCP6-related primary microcephaly by describing cases with severe cortical malformations but without chorioretinopathy, a feature previously considered part of the core phenotype. The authors also provide insights into variant interpretation, noting that most previously reported cases carried at least one loss-of-function allele. The work refines genotype-phenotype correlations for this rare neurodevelopmental disorder.

papers.title: Enhanced prognosis stratification following surgery for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma to optimize clinical decisions by reflecting tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has an extremely dismal postoperative prognosis. Conventional TNM staging cannot adequately characterize tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment, leading to suboptimal risk stratification. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an integrated prognostic system for PDAC by combining deep learning (DL)-based radiomic features with guideline‑recommended clinicopathological variables.
papers.summary: This study develops and externally validates an integrated prognostic system for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma that combines deep learning-derived radiomic features with standard clinicopathological variables. The goal is to improve postoperative risk stratification beyond conventional TNM staging by capturing tumor heterogeneity and microenvironment characteristics.

papers.title: Intra-DNA k-mer conservation patterns encode evolutionary selection of variants.
papers.abstract: Current approaches to variant effect prediction center on protein function and interspecies conservation, largely ignoring cues embedded in local nucleotide composition. We developed kGain, a metric that quantifies how a point mutation reshapes oligonucleotide frequency relative to the host genome. In Escherichia coli and Saccharomyces cerevisiae long-term evolution data, fixed, essential-gene, and recurrent mutations carry elevated kGain values that grow more pronounced over successive generations. Parallel trends appear in SARS-CoV-2 variants of concern and in a bottleneck resistance experim
papers.summary: The authors introduce kGain, a metric that measures how a point mutation alters local oligonucleotide (k-mer) frequencies relative to the host genome. Across E. coli and S. cerevisiae long-term evolution experiments, fixed, essential-gene, and recurrent mutations show elevated kGain values that increase over generations, and similar patterns appear in SARS-CoV-2 variants and a resistance evolution experiment. This suggests that intra-DNA k-mer composition encodes selection signals that complement protein- and conservation-based variant effect prediction.

papers.title: Beyond Mutations: A Seven-CpG DNA Methylation Signature for Predicting HRD in MMRd Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: We previously identified a high level of molecular heterogeneity within mismatch repair deficiency (MMRd) colorectal cancer (CRC). Despite MMRd CRC being typically considered suitable for immunotherapy, only less than half of the metastatic CRC (mCRC) patients achieve complete remission. Thus, the search for identifying new therapeutic targets has become extremely urgent. The use of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi) has revolutionized the treatment of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) cancer; however, the HRD prevalence in CRC remains unclear. Here, we conducted an integra
papers.summary: This study identifies a seven-CpG DNA methylation signature that predicts homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) in mismatch repair-deficient colorectal cancer, extending beyond mutation-based HRD detection. The signature could help identify MMRd CRC patients who might benefit from PARP inhibitors, addressing the heterogeneity in immunotherapy response.

papers.title: Automated Chest Diseases Classification Using Multimodal Deep Learning.
papers.abstract: Computer-Aided Diagnosis systems can support physicians by reducing workload, medical errors, and time required for patient care. However, many existing systems primarily rely on medical images while overlooking valuable information available in associated medical reports. This study proposes a multimodal deep learning approach for chest disease classification by integrating chest X-ray images and radiology reports from the MIMIC-CXR dataset. (2) Methods: Different Deep Learning models are evaluated for each modality, followed by a comprehensive comparison of intermediate and late fusion strat
papers.summary: This study develops a multimodal deep learning system that combines chest X-ray images with their corresponding radiology reports to classify chest diseases, using the MIMIC-CXR dataset. The authors benchmark several deep learning models per modality and compare intermediate versus late fusion strategies for integrating the two data types. The work aims to show that incorporating report text alongside images can improve automated diagnosis compared with image-only systems.

papers.title: Treatment Selection in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Conceptual Framework for Precision Therapy.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains a major therapeutic challenge, with limited improvement in outcomes and substantial heterogeneity in treatment response. Systemic chemotherapy remains a cornerstone of treatment across disease stages, yet treatment selection, particularly in metastatic PDAC (mPDAC), is still driven predominantly by clinical characteristics, performance status, prior therapy, and a limited number of molecular biomarkers. The emergence of biomarker-directed therapies, including strategies targeting oncogenic KRAS alterations, demonstrates the potential of molecular
papers.summary: This review proposes a conceptual framework for moving pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma treatment beyond clinical factors toward precision oncology. It highlights emerging biomarker-directed strategies, particularly those targeting oncogenic KRAS alterations, as a path to reducing treatment heterogeneity and improving outcomes in metastatic disease.

papers.title: Multicenter CT-Based Deep Learning for Preoperative Nodal Risk Stratification in Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Accurate preoperative risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) remains difficult. We developed and validated ThyLNT, a Transformer-based 2.5D deep learning model using preoperative computed tomography (CT), and explored related biological features in multi-omics analyses.
papers.journal: Thyroid : official journal of the American Thyroid Association
papers.summary: This study developed and validated ThyLNT, a Transformer-based 2.5D deep learning model that uses preoperative CT scans to stratify lymph node metastasis risk in papillary thyroid carcinoma across multiple centers. The authors also linked model predictions to biological features through multi-omics analyses, supporting clinical utility for preoperative decision-making.

papers.title: Integrated Whole-Cell Phage Display and Machine Learning Identify Candidate Targeting Ligands in KRAS-Defined Lung Cancer Contexts.
papers.abstract: Phage display can identify ligands that target distinctive cell surface phenotypes, but selection outputs are often complex and difficult to interpret. Here, we developed an integrated workflow combining phage display biopanning, next-generation sequencing (NGS), machine learning (ML), and flow cytometry to discover short peptide binders associated with genotype-defined cancer contexts. Phage display was performed on lung cancer cell lines representing KRAS wild-type (WT), G12C, G12D, and G12V backgrounds, and experimental outputs were used to train a multimodal probabilistic model. From the r
papers.summary: This study combines whole-cell phage display, next-generation sequencing, machine learning, and flow cytometry to identify short peptide ligands that bind lung cancer cells with specific KRAS mutations (wild-type, G12C, G12D, G12V). The authors train a multimodal probabilistic model on the selection outputs to interpret complex biopanning data and nominate candidate targeting peptides. The approach demonstrates how ML can help deconvolute phage display selections for genotype-specific cancer targeting.

papers.title: Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, auto
papers.summary: This review examines how Toll-like receptors recognize Mycoplasma components such as lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA, triggering NF-κB and MAPK signaling that can both clear infection and drive chronic inflammatory pathology. The authors combine cheminformatics and machine-learning approaches to identify and prioritize potential TLR-targeted therapeutic compounds. The work synthesizes immunopathogenesis with computational drug-discovery strategies for Mycoplasma infections.

papers.title: Large Language Model-Enhanced MFSSG Enables Effective and Accurate Integration Analysis for Microbiome-Metabolome Data.
papers.abstract: The massive volume of paired microbiome and metabolome measurementsgenerated through high-throughput sequencing and mass spectrometryhas created an urgent need for dedicated, integrative analytical pipelines. Existing tools lack the capacity to simultaneously support sample clustering, multi-omics visualization, disease risk stratification, and biological age quantification using matched dual-modal datasets. To overcome this analytical bottleneck, we introduce the matrix factorization with shared and specific graph learning (MFSSG) toolkit: an unsupervised matrix factorization framework that
papers.summary: The authors introduce MFSSG, an unsupervised matrix factorization toolkit enhanced with large language models that integrates paired microbiome and metabolome data. It supports sample clustering, multi-omics visualization, disease risk stratification, and biological age quantification in a single pipeline, addressing a gap in existing tools that cannot handle these tasks simultaneously with matched dual-modal datasets.

papers.title: An EFHD1-associated ADSC niche modulates treatment response in experimental models of ER-positive breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Adipose-derived stem cells (ADSCs) modulate the breast cancer (BC) microenvironment, but their role in endocrine therapy resistance and clinical outcomes remains ill-defined.
papers.summary: This study identifies an adipose-derived stem cell (ADSC) niche associated with the protein EFHD1 that influences how ER-positive breast cancer responds to endocrine therapy in experimental models. The findings suggest that targeting this ADSC niche could help overcome treatment resistance and improve clinical outcomes.

papers.title: A dendritic cell-related prognostic signature in glioma: A multi-omic framework integrating transcriptomics, single-cell profiling, and clinical validation.
papers.abstract: Dendritic cells (DCs) infiltrating the glioma microenvironment can promote antitumor immunity or contribute to immunosuppression and immune escape. This dual role underscores the need to define dendritic cell-related genes (DCRGs) for prognostic assessment. Using transcriptomic and clinical data from glioma cohorts (The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Chinese Glioma Genome Atlas (CGGA)), combined with scRNA-seq analysis, we identified ten pivotal DCRGs (CASP1, CD300LF, CTSB, GPR132, HLA-DQA1, PLCB2, RAC2, SIGLEC9, STAT6, TLR1) associated with patient outcomes. A DCRG-based risk signature, devel
papers.summary: The authors combined bulk transcriptomic data from TCGA and CGGA glioma cohorts with single-cell RNA-seq to identify ten dendritic cell-related genes associated with patient survival, and built a risk signature from these genes. The signature stratifies glioma patients by prognosis and is presented as a multi-omic prognostic framework with clinical validation. The work is a prognostic biomarker study rather than a mechanistic or methodological advance.

papers.title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important cha
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The paper introduces st2sc, a computational method that recovers single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data. It addresses the challenge of deconvolving spot-level signals into per-cell, per-gene expression estimates, improving on existing approaches that struggle with accurate gene-level estimation.

papers.title: Viro-BERT: Whole-genome attention for robust viral pathogen classification from next-generation sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Classifying viral pathogens from next-generation sequencing (NGS) data is central to diagnosis and genomic surveillance. Most deep learning classifiers, however, read only a fixed window at the start of each genome, typically a few hundred to a few thousand base pairs, and so ignore more than 95% of the sequence of large DNA viruses such as monkeypox virus (MPV) and herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1). We refer to this problem as Truncation Blindness. Here we present Viro-BERT, which splits a complete genome into overlapping 512-token windows, encodes each window with a shared DistilBERT encoder, a
papers.summary: Viro-BERT addresses 'Truncation Blindness' in viral pathogen classification by processing complete genomes rather than just the first few hundred to few thousand base pairs. It splits genomes into overlapping 512-token windows, encodes each with a shared DistilBERT encoder, and aggregates window-level representations for whole-genome classification. This enables the model to use the >95% of sequence ignored by fixed-window classifiers, improving classification of large DNA viruses like monkeypox and HSV-1 from NGS data.

papers.title: BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring.
papers.abstract: Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. Geometric likelihood models may generalize poorly when training-set structural coverage is limited. We test whether pretrained biomolecular representations improve scoring under a controlled geometric baseline.
papers.summary: The paper introduces BioLM-Score, a protein-ligand scoring method that conditions a geometric likelihood model on pretrained biomolecular language model representations. It tests whether such language priors improve scoring across affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening under a controlled geometric baseline. The work addresses the challenge of generalizing geometric scoring models when training-set structural coverage is limited.

papers.title: LLM Representations Rival Traditional Predictors and Enhance Multimodal Prediction of APOE4 and Aβ-Burden.
papers.abstract: Spontaneous language offers a scalable, non-invasive approach for identifying biological indicators of preclinical Alzheimer's disease (AD). We examined prediction of APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-β (Aβ) burden using Cookie Theft picture-descriptions from two cohorts, including Hebrew- and English-speakers (IRAP, N=134; and WRAP, N=1,541). Aβ burden was classified across lowest-quartile, median, and highest-quartile cutoffs, capturing accumulation below conventional amyloid-positivity thresholds. We compared embeddings from pretrained large language models (LLMs) to standard cognit
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study shows that embeddings from pretrained large language models applied to Cookie Theft picture descriptions can predict APOE4 carrier status and cerebral amyloid-β burden comparably to traditional predictors, and that combining LLM representations with other modalities improves prediction. The work spans Hebrew- and English-speaking cohorts and captures sub-threshold amyloid accumulation, suggesting spontaneous language is a scalable, non-invasive marker for preclinical Alzheimer's disease.

papers.title: Biologically Inspired Selective Attention for Prostate MRI: A Segmentation-Guided Vision Transformer Framework for Computer-Aided Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is the second most commonly diagnosed malignancy in men, yet interpretation of multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) suffers from substantial inter-observer variability and depends on scarce expert radiologists. Expert readers follow a hierarchical, coarse-to-fine visual strategy: they first localize the prostate gland and then direct focused attention to tissue within it. Inspired by this biological selective-attention mechanism, we propose a segmentation-guided framework in which a modality-aware 3D Vision Transformer (ViT) first delineates the prostate gland from T2-weighted, ADC, and
papers.summary: The authors propose a segmentation-guided 3D Vision Transformer for prostate cancer diagnosis on multiparametric MRI, inspired by how expert radiologists first localize the prostate gland and then focus attention within it. The framework uses a modality-aware ViT to delineate the gland from T2-weighted and ADC images, then directs diagnostic attention to the segmented region. This biologically inspired coarse-to-fine design aims to reduce inter-observer variability and reliance on scarce expert readers.

papers.title: HMB-Net: Synergizing Latent Sequential Dynamics and Local Sequence Motifs for Robust RNA Methylation Prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate site-level identification of RNA post-transcriptional modifications is essential for deciphering epitranscriptomic regulation. However, existing deep learning predictors typically rely on either convolutional filters with limited receptive fields or self-attention mechanisms with quadratic complexity, while parallel hybrid networks often struggle to coordinate global sequence context with local motif sensitivity. Here, we present HMB-Net, an interpretable hybrid framework that couples a Selective State Space Model (Mamba) with a deep Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) netw
papers.summary: HMB-Net is a hybrid deep learning model that combines a Mamba selective state space model with a Bi-LSTM network to predict RNA methylation sites, aiming to capture both long-range sequence context and local motif patterns. The framework is presented as an interpretable predictor that addresses the trade-off between limited receptive fields in CNNs and quadratic complexity in self-attention. It is a methodological contribution to epitranscriptomic site prediction rather than a new biological finding.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Protein-Ligand Binding Site Prediction from Protein Sequence and SMILES.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of protein-ligand binding sites is critical for mechanistic biology and drug discovery, yet predictive performance varies substantially across ligand families and data-availability regimes. We present a systematic ligand-aware benchmark and evaluation framework for residue-level binding-site prediction across three settings: overrepresented ligands with abundant examples, underrepresented ligands with limited examples, and zero-shot ligands unseen during training. Using a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering, we evaluate a progressive three-s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces a ligand-aware benchmark for predicting protein-ligand binding sites at the residue level, evaluating models across three regimes: ligands with abundant training data, underrepresented ligands, and zero-shot ligands never seen during training. The framework uses a BioLiP2-derived dataset with ligand-specific sequence clustering to systematically assess how predictive performance varies by ligand family and data availability. It aims to expose where current methods fail and to enable more rigorous, generalizable evaluation of binding-site predictors.

papers.title: GAC-BiT-CNN: A Hybrid Generative Adversarial Capsule-Transformer-CNN Model with Fused Protein Language Model Embeddings for Methyltransferase Prediction.
papers.abstract: Methyltransferases (MTs) are a functionally diverse class of enzymes that catalyse methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM) to DNA, RNA, and proteins, thereby regulating epigenetic programming, gene expression, and numerous disease processes. Dysregulation of these enzymes is implicated in a wide spectrum of human cancers and neurodegenerative disorders, making their accurate computational identification a priority in both basic research and drug discovery. We present GAC-BiT-CNN, a novel hybrid deep learning framework integrating Generative Adversarial Capsule Networks (GAC),
papers.summary: The authors present GAC-BiT-CNN, a hybrid deep learning framework that combines generative adversarial capsule networks, a bidirectional transformer, and a CNN, using fused protein language model embeddings to predict methyltransferases from sequence. The model aims to improve computational identification of this enzyme class, which is relevant to epigenetics, cancer, and drug discovery. The abstract is truncated, so reported performance and benchmarking results are not available for assessment.

papers.title: Protify: A Benchmarking Platform Revealing Task Dependence and Homology Leakage in Protein Language Model Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Protein Language Models (pLMs) have become essential tools for computational protein analysis, and the rapid proliferation of architectures, training objectives, and pretraining corpora has produced a diverse and expanding model landscape. Evaluation practices, however, remain fragmented: studies use different datasets, preprocessing pipelines, and reporting conventions, so results rarely transfer between publications. Here we introduce Protify, an open-source platform that standardizes pLM benchmarking across zero-shot, supervised, and transfer-learning settings through a unified, low-code in
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Protify is an open-source benchmarking platform that standardizes evaluation of protein language models across zero-shot, supervised, and transfer-learning settings, addressing fragmented practices in the field. The platform reveals that model performance is highly task-dependent and that homology leakage between training and test sets can inflate results, highlighting the need for careful benchmark design.

papers.title: A protein language model for domain, functional site, and variant effect prediction.
papers.abstract: Protein sequence databases are growing far faster than experimentally curated annotations, limiting functional interpretation of newly identified proteins and coding variants. We developed PALM, a protein annotation language model that jointly predicts domain and functional-site occurrence, while preserving overlapping and nested annotations through a soft-target objective. PALM integrates ESM2 with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), learned layer aggregation, and a bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) encoder. PALM was trained on ∼15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences spanning 17
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: PALM is a protein language model that combines ESM2 embeddings with LoRA fine-tuning, learned layer aggregation, and a BiLSTM encoder to jointly predict protein domains and functional sites, while allowing overlapping and nested annotations via a soft-target objective. Trained on ~15 million InterPro-annotated UniRef50 sequences, it aims to close the gap between rapidly growing sequence databases and scarce experimental annotations, and is also applied to variant effect prediction.

papers.title: AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free enrichment reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence in malignant effusions.
papers.abstract: Malignant effusions are clinically accessible yet underutilized sources of metastatic tumor cells. However, abundant background immune cells complicate tumor cell isolation and molecular characterization. We integrate AI-powered single-cell imaging and morphology-guided label-free tumor cell enrichment with genomic profiling to characterize phenotypic and genomic heterogeneity in malignant effusions.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint presents an integrated workflow combining AI-powered single-cell imaging with morphology-guided, label-free enrichment to isolate tumor cells from malignant effusions, which are typically dominated by background immune cells. The enriched cells are then genomically profiled to reveal tumor heterogeneity, genomic relatedness, and divergence. The approach demonstrates that clinically accessible effusions can be leveraged for single-cell phenotypic and genomic characterization of metastatic disease.

papers.title: Synthetic MPRA perturbation supervision improves variant-effect prediction in sequence-to-function models.
papers.abstract: Deep learning sequence-to-function (S2F) models learn to predict functional readouts, such as gene expression, from genetic sequence. However, these models are trained predominantly on the reference genome and struggle to accurately predict the effect of genetic variation on gene expression. Massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) explore the direct impact of genetic variation on gene expression, but saturation-mutagenesis MPRAs that measure variant effects directly remain limited, thereby restricting their use for fine-tuning S2F models. In this work, we investigate fine-tuning Borzoi, a s
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors show that fine-tuning the sequence-to-function model Borzoi on synthetic MPRA perturbation data improves its ability to predict the effects of genetic variants on gene expression. Because saturation-mutagenesis MPRAs are scarce, they generate synthetic perturbation supervision to bridge the gap between reference-genome training and variant-effect prediction. This offers a practical route to better variant-effect models without needing large experimental MPRA datasets.

papers.title: Predicting single-molecule chromatin distribution from DNA sequence.
papers.abstract: Genome regulation unfolds through dynamic and stochastic single-molecule events. Deep learning models that read gene regulatory activities from DNA sequences have markedly advanced our ability to predict cell-population-level averages. However, they cannot capture the full spectrum of heterogeneity and dynamics at the single-molecule level, which directly reflect the underlying mechanisms of genome regulation. Here, we introduce a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) framework that directly models the entire probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states from DNA sequence alone. We u
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) deep learning framework that predicts the full probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states directly from DNA sequence, rather than only population-level averages. This enables modeling of heterogeneity and stochastic dynamics in genome regulation that conventional sequence-to-activity models cannot capture.

papers.title: VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq.
papers.abstract: Gene activity quantification from single-cell ATAC-seq is challenging because genomic regions informative of cell identity can vary across genes and tissues, while broadly accessible regions may provide limited cell-type-discriminative information. We developed VIGAT, a vision-language model (VLM)-guided tool that automates visual interpretation of ATAC coverage plots for adaptive gene activity quantification. VIGAT jointly examines accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes, integrating genomic annotations and biological context to select gene-specific regions enriched for cluster-di
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: VIGAT is a new tool that uses a vision-language model to automatically interpret ATAC-seq coverage plots and quantify gene activity from single-cell ATAC-seq data. It adaptively selects gene-specific genomic regions enriched for cell-type-discriminative information by jointly examining accessibility patterns across multiple marker genes and integrating genomic annotations and biological context. This addresses the challenge that informative regulatory regions vary across genes and tissues, improving gene activity quantification.

papers.title: Computational immunogenicity prediction for mRNA vaccines: benchmarks, bottlenecks, and the peptide-nucleotide gap.
papers.abstract: Computational prediction of T-cell epitopes has become indispensable to vaccine design, yet the field still relies on the assumption that how much of a given antigen is produced is fixed by its coding sequence. However, this is not the case with mRNA vaccines, i.e. the design of the mRNA template can vastly alter the quantity of the same protein produced. Codon usage, guanine-cytosine (GC) content, untranslated-region (UTR) design, and predicted secondary structure together define how fast the message is translated and how long it survives, and therefore how much antigen ever reaches the prese
papers.summary: This review argues that computational T-cell epitope prediction for mRNA vaccines is fundamentally limited because it assumes antigen abundance is fixed by the coding sequence, when in reality mRNA design choices—codon usage, GC content, UTR design, and secondary structure—dramatically alter how much protein is actually produced. The authors highlight a 'peptide-nucleotide gap': existing immunogenicity predictors work at the peptide level and ignore these mRNA-level expression determinants, and they benchmark current tools while identifying key bottlenecks that must be addressed to make prediction reliable for mRNA vaccine design.

papers.title: Transformer models in genomics: from sequence analysis to population genetics and biodiversity.
papers.abstract: Modern genomics and artificial intelligence converge at a breakthrough point with the emergence of transformer-based large language models for genomic analysis. This review examines how transformer-based models have advanced genomic sequence analysis through novel tokenization strategies, self-attention mechanisms, and pre-training/fine-tuning paradigms. Unlike prior broad surveys, we focus on three sub-areas of genomics where transformer architectures have had a substantive impact: sequence-level analysis, population-level genetics, including genetic imputation and genome-wide association ana
papers.summary: This review examines how transformer-based large language models are being applied to genomic sequence analysis, focusing on tokenization strategies, self-attention mechanisms, and pre-training/fine-tuning paradigms. It highlights three areas where these architectures have had substantive impact: sequence-level analysis, population genetics (including genetic imputation and GWAS), and biodiversity. The paper distinguishes itself from broader surveys by concentrating on these specific sub-areas.

papers.title: Interaction-finder: automated literature-based discovery of biological entity associations with quote-level provenance.
papers.abstract: Identifying interactions between biological entities is a cornerstone of molecular research, but assembling such lists from the literature is slow and tedious. For many research questions, no curated database exists, leaving researchers to survey the relevant literature themselves. We present interaction-finder, a tool that automates this process: given a topic string and user-defined entity types, it discovers relevant literature through LLM-guided iterative search, extracts candidate associations from full-text articles, and produces a ranked list where every association is backed by quoted
papers.summary: The authors present interaction-finder, a tool that automates literature-based discovery of associations between biological entities. Given a topic and entity types, it uses LLM-guided iterative search to find relevant full-text articles, extracts candidate associations, and returns a ranked list where each association is supported by quoted evidence for provenance. This addresses the gap where no curated database exists for many research questions.

papers.title: Leveraging amino acid embeddings for accurate translation efficiency prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of translation efficiency from messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences is an important step toward mRNA sequence design. In recent years, the widespread adoption of high-resolution ribosome profiling techniques, such as Ribo-seq, has led to rapid accumulation of large-scale datasets that capture the relationship between mRNA sequences and translation efficiency. This progress has facilitated the development of machine-learning-based models for translation efficiency prediction. However, most existing approaches rely primarily on mRNA-derived features, such as codon usage frequency a
papers.summary: This paper introduces a machine-learning approach that incorporates amino acid embeddings—learned representations of the protein sequence encoded by an mRNA—to improve prediction of translation efficiency from mRNA sequences. By moving beyond mRNA-only features like codon usage, the method aims to capture how the resulting protein's properties influence translation. The work supports mRNA sequence design by providing a more accurate predictive model.

papers.title: EV Barcode: A Machine Learning Driven Web Resource for Predicting the Cellular Origin of Extracellular Vesicles From Protein and mRNA Cargo.
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membranous particles secreted by most cell types into the extracellular space, carrying proteins, RNAs, metabolites, and lipids that reflect the physiological state of their cell of origin. Hence, EVs are considered as powerful resource of non-invasive biomarkers for disease diagnosis and prognosis. However, identifying the cellular source of EVs in complex biological samples including blood, urine and milk remains a major challenge, limiting clinical and biological insights. To address this, we developed EV Barcode (https://evbarcode.org/), an open-source web
papers.summary: The authors present EV Barcode, an open-source web resource that uses machine learning to predict the cellular origin of extracellular vesicles based on their protein and mRNA cargo. This addresses a key bottleneck in EV research—identifying which cell type released EVs found in complex biofluids like blood, urine, and milk—which is essential for using EVs as non-invasive disease biomarkers.

papers.title: Handshake: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction at scale using ProstT5 and cross-chain attention.
papers.abstract: Partner-specific protein-protein binding site prediction, identifying which residues of a protein form the interface when bound to a specific partner, remains a challenging task with significant implications for drug discovery and understanding of protein structure and function. Existing computational methods are limited by small training datasets, inconsistent redundancy filtering, and reliance on three-dimensional structural information at test time. Here we present a sequence-only, partner-specific protein-protein interface predictor called HandShake. It combines ProstT5, a protein language
papers.summary: HandShake is a sequence-only computational tool that predicts which residues of a protein form the binding interface with a specific partner, without requiring 3D structural data at test time. It combines the ProstT5 protein language model with cross-chain attention to capture partner-specific interactions, addressing limitations of prior methods such as small training sets and inconsistent redundancy filtering.

papers.title: ADCCR: Adaptive Description Composition and Coarse-to-Fine Refinement for Language-Guided Human Keypoint Localization.
papers.abstract: Biological vision integrates cues according to their reliability and context and uses coarse contextual information to form initial hypotheses before directing attention to local evidence. Inspired by these principles, we propose ADCCR (Adaptive Description Composition and Coarse-to-Fine Refinement), a language-guided framework for flexible human keypoint localization. A multi-granularity bank describes each keypoint by its name, anatomical definition, inter-joint relation, and visual appearance. A reliability-aware composer predicts sample-specific gates from the person image, target identity
papers.summary: ADCCR is a language-guided framework for localizing human keypoints (joints) in images, inspired by how biological vision combines cues by reliability and refines coarse hypotheses with local evidence. It uses a multi-granularity description bank (keypoint name, anatomical definition, inter-joint relations, visual appearance) and a reliability-aware composer that predicts sample-specific gates to weight these descriptions, followed by coarse-to-fine refinement. The work is a methodological contribution to vision-language keypoint localization rather than a biological or omics study.

papers.title: Sex-Specific Plasma Proteomic Signatures in Venous Thromboembolism: Differential Abundance and Machine-Learning-Based Feature Prioritization.
papers.abstract: Background: Sex differences influence venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk and clinical course, but corresponding differences in circulating proteomic profiles among individuals with established VTE remain incompletely characterized. We investigated female-male differences in the MARTHA plasma proteome and evaluated whether the identified signals formed a reproducible multivariable pattern. Methods: We performed a secondary analysis of the MARTHA plasma proteomics dataset, comprising 1388 participants with VTE (906 females and 482 males) and 376 antibody-derived assays targeting 234 candidate pro
papers.summary: This secondary analysis of the MARTHA plasma proteomics dataset examined sex-specific protein abundance differences among 1,388 individuals with established venous thromboembolism, using 376 antibody-based assays targeting 234 candidate proteins. The authors identified differentially abundant proteins between females and males and applied machine-learning-based feature prioritization to determine whether these signals formed a reproducible multivariable pattern. The work highlights that sex-stratified proteomic analysis may reveal distinct biological signatures underlying VTE in women versus men.

papers.title: A Transformers Analysis Pipeline (TrAP) to Evaluate LINE-1 RNA Sequence Content.
papers.abstract: LINE-1 RNA has emerged as a potential regulator of chromatin organization and gene expression, as well as a candidate readout of cellular and disease-associated states. Accurate measurement of LINE-1 transcript abundance is therefore important for evaluating its regulatory, biomarker, and potential therapeutic relevance. Measurement is challenging in short-read RNA sequencing because similar LINE-1 loci produce ambiguous, multi-mapping reads and LINE-1-associated signal can arise from passive as well as autonomous transcription. We developed the Transformers Analysis Pipeline (TrAP), an alignm
papers.summary: The authors present TrAP, a bioinformatics pipeline that uses transformer-based machine learning to analyze LINE-1 RNA sequences from short-read RNA sequencing data, addressing the problem of multi-mapping reads that make LINE-1 transcript quantification difficult. The pipeline aims to improve measurement of LINE-1 transcript abundance, which is relevant as a potential regulator of chromatin and gene expression and as a disease biomarker.

papers.title: Identification of hub genes involved in the pathogenesis of ulcerative colitis: a multi-omics study integrating machine learning, Mendelian randomization, and mediation analysis.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with a steadily increasing global prevalence, yet its precise molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify potential diagnostic biomarkers for UC and explore potential metabolite-mediated pathways linking gene expression to UC.
papers.summary: This study combines differential expression analysis, machine learning, Mendelian randomization, and mediation analysis across multi-omics data to identify hub genes associated with ulcerative colitis and to test whether metabolites mediate the link between gene expression and disease risk. It nominates candidate diagnostic biomarkers and proposes metabolite-mediated pathways, though the findings are computational and require experimental validation.

papers.title: GPCRVS in the detection of target-selective molecular scaffolds based on deep learning and gradient boosting.
papers.abstract: High drug selectivity minimizes unintended interactions that cause adverse effects, decreases drug potency, and are failure-prone factors in many clinical trials due to a poor balance between drug efficacy and toxicity. Sharing similar structural folds and modes of activation, G protein-coupled receptors (GPCR) may represent difficult drug targets in terms of optimization of pharmacodynamic profiles towards drug target selectivity. Here, we describe GPCRVS, a web service for GPCR virtual screening, designed to detect selective drug-like compounds. GPCRVS combines machine learning for ligand-ba
papers.summary: GPCRVS is a new web service that combines deep learning and gradient boosting to virtually screen chemical compounds for selective binding to G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), a large family of drug targets where achieving selectivity is notoriously difficult. The tool aims to help identify drug-like molecules that preferentially hit one GPCR over closely related ones, potentially reducing side effects and improving clinical success rates.

papers.title: Self-Attention-Based Deep-Learning Model Using Multimodal MRI to Predict Ki-67 Expression and Recurrence-Free Survival in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To assess multimodal gadolinium-enhanced MRI-based deep learning fusion schemes for preoperative Ki-67 expression estimation in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and clarify their correlation with recurrence-free survival (RFS).
papers.summary: This study develops a self-attention-based deep-learning model that fuses multimodal gadolinium-enhanced MRI to preoperatively predict Ki-67 expression in hepatocellular carcinoma. The predicted Ki-67 status is then linked to recurrence-free survival, suggesting a non-invasive imaging biomarker for tumor proliferation and prognosis.

papers.title: Integrated Bioinformatic Analysis and Preliminary Clinical Validation Reveal a Candidate Diagnostic Immune-Related Gene Signature for Chronic Endometritis.
papers.abstract: Chronic endometritis (CE) is an underdiagnosed condition linked to female infertility. Its immune-related gene (IRG) signature and the mechanisms underlying its immune microenvironment remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates public transcriptomic datasets with bioinformatic analyses to identify an immune-related gene signature for chronic endometritis, a condition associated with infertility that is often underdiagnosed. The authors then perform preliminary clinical validation of the candidate genes, aiming to clarify the immune microenvironment mechanisms underlying the disease. The work proposes a diagnostic gene panel, though validation is limited and preliminary.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in influenza prevention and control: translational pathways, supporting evidence, and system-level challenges.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to influenza prevention and control. AI encompasses conventional machine learning, deep learning, and protein language models. Large language models (LLMs) are an emerging subset of AI. Current evidence remains weakly linked to real-world workflows and population health outcomes. This structured narrative review proposes a three-stage translational maturity framework. Phase I is technical efficacy assessment. Phase II is implementation effectiveness verification. Phase III is population impact and sustainability. We synthesized evidence in t
papers.summary: This structured narrative review examines how AI is being applied to influenza prevention and control, covering conventional machine learning, deep learning, protein language models, and emerging LLMs. The authors argue that current evidence is only weakly connected to real-world public health workflows and population outcomes, and they propose a three-stage translational maturity framework (technical efficacy, implementation effectiveness, and population impact/sustainability) to organize and evaluate the field.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Guided Precision Nanomedicine: Bridging Delivery Barriers, Controlled Release, and Clinical Translation.
papers.abstract: Targeted drug delivery aims to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity, yet its clinical translation remains limited by the unpredictable in vivo behaviour of nanocarriers. Although a broad range of nanocarrier platforms-including lipid-, polymer-, protein-, inorganic- and biomimetic-based systems-can improve drug solubility, pharmacokinetics, lesion-site accumulation and controlled release, their performance is frequently constrained by heterogeneous disease biology, insufficient tissue penetration, premature clearance, immune recognition and manufacturing variability.
papers.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence can guide the design and clinical translation of nanomedicine drug delivery systems. It argues that AI can help overcome persistent barriers such as unpredictable in vivo behavior, poor tissue penetration, immune recognition, and manufacturing variability that have limited the clinical success of nanocarriers. The paper synthesizes AI approaches for optimizing nanocarrier design, predicting biological behavior, and enabling controlled release toward more reliable clinical translation.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation reveal PFAS-associated immune-inflammatory signatures in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants increasingly implicated in respiratory disorders. However, the systems-level connections among PFAS-associated molecular perturbations, immune dysregulation, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to prioritize candidate links between PFAS-associated target information and COPD-related transcriptional and inflammatory signatures.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data, machine learning, and computational toxicology to identify molecular connections between PFAS exposure and COPD, then validates key findings experimentally. The authors prioritize candidate PFAS-associated targets that overlap with COPD-related transcriptional and immune-inflammatory signatures, suggesting mechanistic links between these environmental contaminants and respiratory disease.

papers.title: Physiological proxies of feed efficiency in pigs: exploring the predictive value of blood biochemical and hematological profiles.
papers.abstract: Developing strategies to improve feed efficiency can help the swine industry become more sustainable while meeting the worldwide demand for pork products, yet most commercial barns cannot practically calculate direct metrics of individual feed efficiency. Physiological indicators of metabolic pathways can serve as intermediate variables to predict performance outcomes and, therefore, as biomarkers of feed efficiency and other desirable production traits in growing pigs. This research aimed to assess the role of conventional blood parameters as proxies for performance outcomes and their predict
papers.summary: This study evaluated whether routine blood biochemical and hematological measurements can serve as practical proxies for feed efficiency in growing pigs, since direct measurement of individual feed intake is impractical in commercial barns. The authors assessed conventional blood parameters as intermediate physiological indicators of metabolic pathways and tested their predictive value for performance outcomes. The work aims to support biomarker-based selection for improved feed efficiency and sustainability in swine production.

papers.title: A Machine-Learning Framework Integrating Frequency-Domain Spectral Features for Ligand Classification and Candidate Prioritization.
papers.abstract: AI-assisted drug discovery (AIDD) combines molecular modeling with machine learning to support lead identification and candidate prioritization. Conventional molecular descriptors principally encode static chemical structures, leaving frequency-domain behavior as an additional source of molecular information. We therefore developed the terahertz fusion descriptor (THz-FD), a feature-fusion framework that integrates terahertz (THz) frequency-domain features for Na+/K+-ATPase ligand classification and retrospective ranking. Extra Trees (ET), Random Forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) c
papers.summary: The authors introduce THz-FD, a machine-learning framework that fuses conventional molecular descriptors with terahertz frequency-domain spectral features to classify Na+/K+-ATPase ligands and prioritize drug candidates. Using Extra Trees, Random Forest, and SVM classifiers, they show that adding frequency-domain information improves ligand classification and retrospective ranking compared with structure-only descriptors. The work suggests frequency-domain molecular behavior can serve as a complementary feature source in AI-assisted drug discovery.

papers.title: Integrative ferroptosis-related bioinformatics identifies PPARγ as a therapeutic target of ursolic acid against inflammation and pathological osteogenesis in ankylosing spondylitis.
papers.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease characterized by persistent inflammation and aberrant new bone formation. Ferroptosis has increasingly been implicated in immune dysregulation and pathological bone remodeling; however, its molecular involvement in AS and its potential value for natural product discovery remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify ferroptosis-related molecular targets in AS, screen natural compounds targeting the key candidate, and validate their therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrated ferroptosis-related bioinformatics with natural compound screening to identify PPARγ as a key target in ankylosing spondylitis, then validated ursolic acid as a compound that acts through PPARγ to reduce inflammation and pathological bone formation. The work links ferroptosis biology to AS pathology and proposes a natural-product therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Medical-oriented multi-label diagnosis of twelve-lead ECG signals via disease-aware relational modeling and pathology-aware temporal evidence aggregation.
papers.abstract: Twelve-lead ECG signals are of great value in cardiovascular disease screening and assisted diagnosis, but their multi-label recognition process is simultaneously affected by cross-lead structural dependencies, disease label co-occurrence relationships, and the dispersed distribution of pathological evidence in long-sequence signals. To address these issues, this study proposes a deep learning model for twelve-lead ECG multi-label diagnosis. The model adopts a Transformer-Mamba hybrid structure as the temporal encoding backbone to extract local waveform variations and long-range rhythm feature
papers.summary: The paper proposes a deep learning model for multi-label diagnosis from twelve-lead ECG signals, combining a Transformer-Mamba hybrid temporal encoder with disease-aware relational modeling and pathology-aware temporal evidence aggregation. It aims to capture cross-lead dependencies, label co-occurrence, and dispersed pathological evidence across long sequences. The work is a methodological contribution to automated ECG interpretation.

papers.title: Machine learning prediction of 1-year thrombosis risk in membranous nephropathy: integration of renal pathology and early longitudinal trajectories.
papers.abstract: Patients with membranous nephropathy (MN) have an increased risk of thrombotic events. Existing prediction approaches primarily use clinical and laboratory measurements obtained at a single time point and rarely incorporate renal pathology or early longitudinal changes. This study integrated multiple types of information to predict the occurrence of thrombosis from 4 weeks after discharge to 1 year after being diagnosed with MN.
papers.summary: This study builds a machine learning model to predict thrombotic events within one year of a membranous nephropathy diagnosis, combining renal pathology features with early longitudinal clinical trajectories rather than single-timepoint lab values. The integration of pathology and early change data is proposed to improve risk stratification over existing single-snapshot approaches. The abstract does not report performance metrics or validation results.

papers.title: A machine learning-assisted hypoxia-associated prognostic model reveals PFKP-mediated glycolytic regulation in uveal melanoma.
papers.abstract: Uveal melanoma (UM) is a highly aggressive intraocular malignancy with strong metastatic propensity and poor response to immunotherapy. Hypoxia profoundly reshapes the tumor microenvironment and drives immune evasion. This study aimed to develop a machine learning-assisted hypoxia-related prognostic model and identify relevant metabolic candidates associated with UM progression.
papers.summary: The authors built a machine learning-based prognostic model from hypoxia-related genes to stratify uveal melanoma patients by risk, then identified PFKP, a glycolytic enzyme, as a candidate driving tumor progression under hypoxic conditions. The work links hypoxia-driven metabolic reprogramming to immune microenvironment remodeling in this aggressive eye cancer.

papers.title: Selective representation learning boosts intrinsically disordered protein prediction from pretrained language models.
papers.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins and intrinsically disordered regions lack stable tertiary structures yet play indispensable roles in cellular signaling, regulation, and disease processes. Predicting disorder from sequence alone remains a fundamental challenge in computational biology. Recent advances in pretrained protein language models have shown great potential in capturing rich contextual representations. However, hierarchical pretrained protein language model features suffer from token-level noise and multi-layer redundancy, which limits their efficacy in downstream tasks.
papers.summary: This paper addresses the problem that pretrained protein language models produce noisy and redundant token-level features across their layers, which limits their usefulness for predicting intrinsically disordered proteins and regions. The authors propose a selective representation learning approach that chooses which features to use, and show it improves disorder prediction from sequence alone. The work is a targeted methodological contribution to computational disorder prediction rather than a broad new resource.

papers.title: The predictive dermatome: a technical framework for spatial AI mapping of molecular skin aging.
papers.abstract: Skin aging is spatially heterogeneous. Chronological age and most systemic aging clocks provide useful population-level estimates, but they do not explain why adjacent or anatomically distinct skin regions may show different rates of dermal thinning, matrix remodeling, pigmentation change, vascular fragility, inflammation, or treatment response. We define the Predictive Dermatome as a computationally derived, anatomically localized skin region characterized by a shared or probabilistically related biological aging state and trajectory inferred from integrated molecular, structural, imaging, cl
papers.summary: This paper proposes the 'Predictive Dermatome' as a conceptual and technical framework for using spatial AI to map molecular skin aging. It argues that skin aging is spatially heterogeneous, so population-level aging clocks cannot capture why different skin regions age at different rates, and it outlines how integrated molecular, structural, and imaging data could define anatomically localized regions with shared aging trajectories. The work is primarily a framework proposal rather than an empirical study.

papers.title: ToxiFusion: integrating contextual and compositional sequence representations for toxic peptide prediction.
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting of toxic peptides from sequence information is important for peptide safety assessment and therapeutic development. However, reported performance of computational predictors can be affected by representation limitations and evaluation bias.
papers.summary: ToxiFusion introduces a computational framework for predicting toxic peptides from sequence alone by combining contextual and compositional sequence representations, aiming to improve peptide safety assessment and therapeutic development. The authors also highlight that reported performance of existing predictors can be inflated by representation limitations and evaluation bias, motivating a more robust modeling approach.
